method: After freezing the decision and canonical record, returned to the downloaded 2026–2027 programme regulations and the current official thesis and preparation entries. Rebuilt the major credit breakdown and checked entry progression. Separately reconsidered the current UCR workbook’s literary content, course placements and the differences among plans against the final record. This is a separate same-AI pass.
findings: The Dutch registration has a 120 EC major and 60 EC profiling. The two foundational packages, philosophy course and research seminar account for 75 EC of required coursework. The 7.5 EC thesis, 30 EC depth package and 7.5 EC restricted context choice complete the major. Appendix 2 lists Performing Arts and Creative Technologies and Kunst, cultuur en maatschappij first in their respective lists. Appendix 7 confirms that the depth package is taught and assessed in English within the Dutch track. The four advanced depth courses, research seminar and thesis total 45 EC at level 3, meeting the major minimum. Profiling includes a coherent 30 EC package; external or atypical choices may require approval. No placement is compulsory in the illustrated route.

Finish the two foundation packages in Year 1. Year 2 combines the depth courses in Blocks 1–4 with the context choice in Block 1, philosophy in Block 2 and profiling in Blocks 3 and 4. Year 3 begins with the seminar in Block 1 and thesis in Block 2, or repeats the pair in Blocks 3 and 4. The completed Year 2 depth package satisfies the seminar’s 22.5 EC advanced requirement and three-pass expectation. The thesis uses a passed proposal; the current thesis planner retains the predecessor seminar code MC3V14001, while the 2026–2027 OER and current seminar planner identify its replacement ME3V26011. First-year progression requires 45 of 60 EC under the published BSA.

The broad plan directly supports film, adaptation, visual analysis, museum interpretation and related historical inquiry. It has only limited creative performance practice, and dedicated theater, dance, philosophy of science and a compulsory thesis are visible gaps. The participatory plan responds to co-creation, fan cultures and green media through documentary production, TV and social platforms, participatory qualitative methods and public persuasion; governance adds stakeholder participation and climate policy rather than claiming professional media-industry management. The digital plan builds critical media inquiry with AI bias and accountability, digital misinformation, data analysis, databases and computational imaging; it does not reproduce Utrecht’s specialist treatment of global platform industries. The historical research seminar is a partial research-method correspondence, not a Utrecht thesis preparation course. Heritage was evaluated through media archaeology, museum interpretation, documentary and art history, substantially shared with the broad option. A fourth performance plan would lack a sustained performance and dance sequence. The three options remain substantively distinct.
